Marta / team — quick sizing draft below (high level math, will sync into spreadsheet).

Assumptions from helix_initial_profile.csv: mean tokens/request ~ 120, tokens/sec per GPU (A100 80GB mixed precision) ~ 1,200 for our quantized workload.

1) Token-rate conversion:
- Steady: 650 req/s * 120 tok = 78k tok/s -> ~65 GPUs (78k / 1.2k)
- 95th: 1,800 req/s * 120 = 216k tok/s -> ~180 GPUs

2) Safety and warm-up: aim for 20% spare capacity for warm-KV cache and batching efficiency -> round up GPUs by 20%: steady ~78 GPUs, 95th ~216 GPUs.

3) Admission & janitor thresholds:
- Soft admission: cap per-GPU inflight requests so queue depth per device <= 250 requests.
- Janitor eviction: clear cold-KV entries older than 10 minutes and throttle long-running sessions after 5s tail latency spikes.

4) Autoscale policy suggestion:
- Fast path: scale by slab (8–16 GPUs) when 2-minute moving-average token-rate > slab capacity * 0.75.
- Backoff: maintain slab at least 6 minutes to avoid thrash.

5) Networking (preliminary): at 216 GPUs worst-case, egress expected ~28–32 Gbps for payload/body traffic; allow headroom to 45 Gbps including management traffic.

I ran a quick admission simulation attached (k8s-admission-sim-results.csv) showing expected queueing and p95 latency under three workload shapes. Happy to walk through the numbers on the call.

—Laura
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: k8s-admission-sim-results.csv

Marta — networking notes to include in the handoff doc (specific to Helix VPC peering):

- MTU: set to 9000 on the GPU subnet and ensure path MTU across peering links. Fragmentation causes ~12–18% CPU overhead on some routers for RPC-heavy workloads.
- Peering topology: prefer full-mesh between inference and analytics VPCs in the same AZ; cross-AZ peering increases latency variance.
- NAT / Egress sizing: plan for two active 25 Gbps NAT gateways + one standby for HA if your peak egress approaches 40 Gbps.
- Security: we recommend private link for control-plane telemetry to avoid egress charges and to keep trace payloads within customer backbone.

Network artifacts added: network-diagram.png (sketch for peered VPC layout), brief SLA draft (sla-draft-helix.pdf) with proposed throughput and maintenance windows.

I can add a short checklist itemizing the validations your infra team needs to do during staging: MTU test, throughput soak (48 hours), and peering failover drill.

—Naomi
Network Architect, Redwood Inference
